prerequisites: It is strongly recommended to have passed the subjects of Manufacturing Engineering and Elasticity and Strength of Materials.

learning_outcomes.text: That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by means of the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Knowledge and skills for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Knowledge and skills to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge and skills for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
Knowledge and skills for the design, analysis and calculation of mechanisms and mechanical systems.
Ability for oral and written transmission of information adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies including information and communication technologies.
Ability for information management, handling and application of technical specifications and necessary legislation for engineering practice.

syllabus_topics: Molding and sintering forming processes
Plastic deformation forming processes
Material removal forming processes
Joining forming processes
Dimensional metrology
Quality control of manufacturing processes
Topic 1. Metrology. Introduction to metrology. International System of Units. Measurement and uncertainty calculation in measurement. Dimensional and Geometric Tolerances. Tolerance Chains.
Topic 2. Foundry. Casting technology. Fusion. Foundry parameters. Design of patterns and cores.
Topic 3. Plastics forming. Mechanical behavior of plastics. Plastics extrusion process. Plastics injection process.
Topic 4. Particle forming process. Fundamentals. Particle technology. Characteristics of the particles used. Compaction. Sintering.

Topic 5. Volumetric plastic deformation. Fundamentals of plasticity theory, plastification criteria, strain hardening, incremental plasticity theory. Forging analysis. Rolling analysis. Extrusion analysis. Drawing or wire drawing analysis.
Topic 6. Sheet metal forming. Analysis of the cutting operation. Analysis of the bending operation. Analysis of deep drawing.
Topic 7. Conventional machining engineering. Basic concepts. Chip formation model. Forces in chip removal. Cutting temperature. Tool life. Cutting fluids. Machining economy.
Topic 8. Conventional machining processes: turning, milling, drilling. Classification of conventional machining processes. Turning engineering. Milling engineering. Drilling engineering.
Topic 9. Joining and mechanical assembly processes. Welding processes. Adhesive bonding. Mechanical assembly.
Topic 10. Quality in manufacturing. Introduction to quality. Recommendations for quality improvement. Methods for quality improvement. Statistical process control. Ethics in manufacturing.
Practice 1. Measurement of geometric tolerances. Performing form measurements on a part using different measuring instruments. Expression of measurement and geometric tolerances.
Practice 2. Measurement of dimensional tolerances. Practices for measuring dimensional tolerances and estimating measurement quality.

Practice 3. Plastic injection simulation with CAE software. Simulation of plastic injection process with specialized CAE software. Study of the process phases and parameter evolution. PvT diagram representation.

Practice 4. Computer-aided sheet metal forming processes using CAD software. Simulation of different sheet metal forming processes with CAD-CAE software. Design and generation of a sheet metal object.

Practice 5. ISO programming of pocketing operations. Simulation of CNC milling process with specialized CAE software. Design, calculation, programming and simulation of the milling processes necessary for pocketing a prismatic part.
teaching_methods: Lectures: Theoretical classes to provide a systematic overview of the subject's theoretical concepts, highlighting their most important aspects.
Theory exposition and general examples: Problem-solving in class using illustrative example cases to reinforce theoretical foundations and develop necessary skills for mastering the subject.

Practical activities in laboratories and computer labs: Application of course knowledge to practical cases, either by performing practical exercises using traditional calculation methods or with the use of CAD/CAE/CAM software and tools.
Exercise resolution: Application of course knowledge to solve problems.

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical concepts of the subject (Final written exam)

assessment_rules: To pass the subject, a score equal to or greater than 5 out of 10 points is required in the final written exam. It is also a necessary condition to have attended all practical sessions and submitted all required reports or assignments. The overall grade is calculated as 5% for attendance and participation, 70% for the final written exam on theoretical and practical concepts, 5% for assignments, cases, and exercises, and 20% for laboratory and workshop practices.
